question: Carbamazepine and phenytoin are contraindicated as first-line antiepileptic drugs in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) because they can exacerbate myoclonic and absence seizures.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true — and a critical prescribing trap. Both carbamazepine and phenytoin are contraindicated in generalised epilepsy syndromes with myoclonic or absence components (JME, CAE). They worsen seizure frequency. Always confirm the epilepsy syndrome before choosing an AED.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Carbamazepine and phenytoin are sodium-channel blockers that can paradoxically worsen myoclonic and absence seizures (and spike-wave activity). Valproate is the drug of choice for JME, with levetiracetam as an alternative (especially in women of childbearing age given valproate's teratogenicity).
